title: Microburst warmup hedge controller to stabilize TTFT and tokens/sec
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Multiple enterprise customers and hosted tenants reported a sudden regression in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sustained tokens/sec after the runtime-1.18 rollout. Issue spans Hosted (us-west), several Dedicated pools (eu-central), and at least two Private VPC deployments. Symptoms: intermittent microburst-induced token throughput collapse, elevated median TTFT (+180ms), and increased tail variance. Initial triage indicates warmup/batching interaction with the new adaptive batching heuristic and prefetch logic is causing warmup thrashing and KV-cache eviction races. This ticket implements a conservative 'warmup hedge controller' to: (1) detect microburst patterns per deployment/model, (2) hold back a small warmup reservation to stabilize kernel/warmstart behavior, and (3) smooth prefetch pacing to avoid eviction storms. Objective: deliver a cross-deployment hotfix that recovers customer-facing latency and tokens/sec within SLO targets while landing a robust controller for longer-term rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Hosted median TTFT reduced to within 10% of pre-rollout baseline (measured over 24h)
Sustained tokens/sec >= 95% of baseline for affected models over 6h windows
Canary on 10% traffic for 48h with dashboards showing stable kernel selection and KV hit-rate
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Kumar: Initial customer impact call with SEs. Three customers reported regressions after runtime-1.18; attached telemetry shows coupling between warmup spikes and kernel selector thrash. Decided to open P0 and assign for immediate mitigation.

2026-03-10 11:45 - Liang Chen: Ran heap of perf traces from us-west hosted cluster. Observed repeated prefetch/evict cycles correlated with microburst arrival; batching heuristic increases microbatches briefly which triggers aggressive KV eviction. Drafted proof-of-concept for a 'holdback' gating flag to reserve warmup slots.

2026-03-10 15:30 - Tomás Rivera (oncall): Deployed conservative gating to a single dedicated pool as hotpatch (feature flag). Early telemetry: median TTFT dropped ~120ms, tokens/sec improved 8% in test pool. No regressions in error rates seen.
2026-03-11 09:00 - Product: Notified customers of investigation and planned hotfix. Secured approval for cross-deployment canary and agreed on rollback threshold (TTFT reversion >10% for 30m).

2026-03-11 13:22 - Code review (PR#4218): Feedback from runtime team to add metrics hooks (warmup_reservation_used, microburst_detected, prefetch_backpressure) and make the default reservation percentage configurable per model. Liang to address.

2026-03-11 17:05 - QA: Integration tests written for synthetic microburst patterns (burst size/time series). Found an edge where reservation interacts poorly with multiplex scheduling; added a small randomized jitter to admission path.

2026-03-12 08:58 - Liang Chen: Implemented metrics and config, pushed updated PR. Plan: roll canary to 5% hosted + one Dedicated pool + one Private customer (with consent) for 48h. Added rollback automation via release pipeline.
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (hotfix, 24-48h): enable conservative warmup gating behind feature flag; apply to 5-10% canary traffic across Hosted + one Dedicated pool; monitor SLOs and customer signals.
Phase 1 (stabilize, 1 week): finalize warmup hedge controller, add model-level config, integrate prefetch pacing, add metrics/dashboards & alerts.
Phase 2 (rollout, 2-3 weeks): ramp canary to 100% per region with automated rollback thresholds; update runbooks and debrief with affected customers.
Phase 3 (long term): explore adaptive ML hedging and tighter autoscaler integration to avoid manual reservation tuning.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-reserving warmup slots could reduce peak throughput. Mitigation: conservative default (2-5% of concurrency) + canary ramp and telemetry-backed rollback.
Risk: Interaction with Dedicated autoscaler causing oscillation. Mitigation: coordinate with autoscale team (ENG-903345) and add autoscale-aware holdback logic.
Risk: Private customers may have custom kernels/quant configs. Mitigation: run private customer in canary with rollback consent and maintain per-deployment toggles.
Risk: Missing observability for microburst detection. Mitigation: add dedicated metrics and a dashboard for warmup reservation usage and KV-hit correlation.
